ambiguities_or_notes: Tolstoy's opening letter to Yergolskaya is French and is translated directly from French; his separate postscript to Mashenka is Russian and is translated directly from Russian.
The Soviet editors' Russian rendering is translated separately as apparatus and is not substituted for Tolstoy's French wording.
The manuscript address reads masculine 'Его [sic] Высокоблагородию' before Tatyana Yergolskaya's name. The English preserves the anomaly as 'His [sic] High Born' rather than silently correcting it.
The repeated Russian postscript in the editorial rendering is preserved as a repeated apparatus item, as it is present in the audited witness.
Both source-page markers and all six source footnotes are represented.
